comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C1-C2, C10-C16 establishing scientific context and motivation. Both evaluations agree these background claims about limitations of existing methods are well-supported by citations and represent accepted knowledge in the field.

Perfect alignment on claims C54-C57 regarding nanobody properties and technical advantages. Both evaluations agree these methodological context claims are supported by established literature and citations.

Perfect alignment on claims C58-C59 about future possibilities. Both evaluations classify these as UNCERTAIN/speculative, noting they represent proposed future work rather than demonstrated results with no experimental validation provided.

Strong alignment on core MaMBA methodology claims C3-C5, C17-C24. Both evaluations support the innovative nanobody-based approach, enzymatic conjugation strategy, and modular design. OpenEval additionally includes C25 (consistent labeling degree) in this grouping while peer review addresses it separately.

Strong alignment on claims C26-C27 comparing MaMBA to traditional methods. Both evaluations support the superiority claims based on western blot data, though peer review also includes C25 (consistent labeling) in this grouping while OpenEval groups C25 with core methodology.

Strong alignment on high-throughput serology claims C44-C48, C50. Both evaluations support the SARS-CoV-2 IgG detection in large cohorts, sensitivity comparisons, and technical reproducibility metrics. OpenEval additionally includes C7 in this grouping.

Strong alignment on HBV diagnostic claims C51-C53. Both evaluations support the technical reproducibility and diagnostic performance metrics. OpenEval additionally includes C8 in this grouping while peer review focuses on the three core validation claims.

Partial alignment on imaging performance claims C28-C31 regarding signal amplification, resolution preservation, and iterative workflow robustness. Both evaluations support these technical claims. OpenEval groups these with additional claims C6, C32-C35 covering multiplexing and biological applications, while peer review addresses those separately.

Partial alignment on multiplexing capability claims C6, C33-C35. Both evaluations support the 12-plex imaging demonstration and cell-type identification. OpenEval groups these with broader imaging claims C28-C32, while peer review focuses specifically on the multiplexing achievement.

Minimal alignment on claim C32 regarding psoriasis tissue validation. Both evaluations support this biological observation. OpenEval groups it with comprehensive imaging claims C6, C28-C35, while peer review treats it as a standalone confirmatory finding.

Partial alignment on BLISA quantitative performance claims C36-C37. Both evaluations support the validation data and quantitative capabilities. OpenEval groups these with additional claims C38-C41 covering correlation, specificity, and multiplexing, while peer review addresses those separately.

Partial alignment on BLISA validation claims C38-C41 regarding correlation with orthogonal methods, lack of cross-reactivity, and 7-plex detection. Both evaluations support these technical performance claims. OpenEval groups these with C36-C37, while peer review groups them with drug screening claims C42-C43.

Partial alignment on drug screening claims C42-C43 regarding PFK15 identification and ELISA validation. Both evaluations support the multiplexed screening demonstration. OpenEval additionally includes C9 in this grouping, while peer review groups these claims with broader BLISA validation claims C38-C41.

OpenEval uniquely includes claim C25 (consistent labeling degree across conditions) in the core methodology grouping R1, while peer review addresses this claim separately in R2 alongside comparative performance claims.
OpenEval uniquely includes claim C9 in the drug screening grouping R5. This claim is not explicitly addressed in any peer review result grouping.
OpenEval uniquely includes claim C7 in the high-throughput serology grouping R6. This claim is not explicitly addressed in any peer review result grouping.
OpenEval uniquely includes claim C8 in the HBV diagnostic grouping R7. This claim is not explicitly addressed in any peer review result grouping.
